output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses traces mainly to the 12 August relay server move, not to agency staff. The import skipped 11 of 14 forwarding rules, including the 15-second hold-off for brief SpO2 dips, repeat-alarm suppression, and sending technical alarms only to the charge phone. Pods A–C then got about twice the phone notifications per nurse (roughly 38 to 82 per shift), and acknowledgement time doubled. Pod D, still on the old server, saw no change. Within Pods A–C, agency and core nurses have almost identical incident rates. Bedside alarm volume was flat, so acuity and the monitor v7.2 update are not the cause. I'm fairly confident (about 85–90%). Don't approve the agency cap or the performance reviews. They would punish people for a system fault and discourage reporting. Don't switch off phone forwarding either, because the central station is unstaffed at night. Instead, restore the old rules with Clinical Engineering validation and Alarm Committee sign-off, then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. The phone-fails-to-ring reports (e.g. room 14) and the rise in sick leave remain unexplained. The sick leave rise looks partly viral and partly unknown. Check both after the fix.
